lines:
Responsibilities: Is the LocalSqlite implementation of the trusted core LocalHistoryCommitPort. It validates the selected backend and expected stream head, then atomically commits semantic events, attempts, head/version, optional checkpoint, command/invocation deduplication result, and delivery outbox rows.
Owned records/files: command_dedup and invocation_dedup keyed by stable idempotency key and request hash; delivery_outbox keyed by OutboxId with ChatId/commit sequence, payload hash, destination, state, and delivery cursor; transaction/commit receipts and bounded failure counters. Canonical event/checkpoint rows remain owned by the Semantic Ledger.
Keys and ordering: one BEGIN IMMEDIATE writer serializes head advancement per database; duplicate keys with the same request hash return the original durable receipt, while key reuse with different content is rejected. Outbox entries are ordered by commit sequence and OutboxId; delivered marking cannot alter canonical events.
Ports: accepts CommitBatch, VerifyCommit, ListPendingOutbox, and MarkOutboxDelivered only from the core event committer/recovery. It calls LocalLedgerTxnPort and PreparedArtifactRefPort; projection delivery consumes an idempotent committed-outbox cursor. PortableProject bindings are rejected and never mirrored here.
Normative microbatch contract: A CommitBatch preserves semantic proposal order, receives one contiguous sequence range, and validates span start/parent/content/terminal transitions. It rejects parent changes, content before start, duplicate terminals, and a parent terminal with open children. Incremental batches use the same atomic event/head/checkpoint/dedup/outbox transaction as terminal batches. No success acknowledgement or committed-stream publication occurs before COMMIT. The bounded writer supports frequent small live-delta commits while retaining the 64-event/1-MiB hard limit and under-50-ms local p95 target.

Durability/failure rules: prepared artifact bytes must be hash-verified and fsynced before BEGIN; the SQLite transaction writes every relational part and COMMITs before any success acknowledgement. Failure before durable COMMIT rolls back and returns no state transition. An ambiguous COMMIT is resolved on a fresh connection by EventId/dedup key/request hash, never by blindly repeating a possibly side-effecting operation. SQLITE_FULL, I/O error, corruption, or outbox hard limit closes writes with an inspectable reason.
Retention/performance: batches are bounded to 64 semantic events/1 MiB; the single-writer queue is bounded and exposes latency/depth. Dedup rows live at least through the configurable command/invocation retry horizon and are compacted only against terminal-stream checkpoints; outbox rows compact only after acknowledged delivery and safety margin.
Security/non-responsibilities: credential values, raw secrets, hidden reasoning, and unredacted protocol payloads are invalid. The adapter does not select a history backend, make workflow/authority decisions, execute or retry effects, publish uncommitted events, build projections, or write portable JSONL.

data.name: Atomic Commit, Checkpoint, Deduplication & Outbox Adapter
data.technology: Rust SQLite transaction adapter with transactional outbox
